title: The RAG Stack We Landed On After 37 Fails - Jonathan Fernandes
talk_summary: A RAG tutorial walking through a naive LlamaIndex pipeline then adding query processing, a bi-encoder for retrieval plus a cross-encoder reranker post-retrieval, and tracing/eval tooling (Arize Phoenix, Ragas). The only substantive mechanism is the retrieve-then-rerank split and the insistence on an eval harness over single-question eyeballing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a fast, scalable bi-encoder to pull a candidate set from the vector store, then a slower cross-encoder reranker over just those few candidates to reorder by semantic relevance before stuffing context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cross encoder would be a really good solution post the vector database and so post retrieval
takeaways.numbers: reranked top 2 results; retrieved 5 candidates first

takeaways.technique: Eval harness instead of single-example testing
takeaways.what_they_do: Replace ad-hoc single-question checking with a framework (Ragas) that scores the pipeline across many documents and multiple quality dimensions, using an LLM as judge.
Instrument each pipeline stage (retrieval, rerank, LLM) with tracing (Arize Phoenix/LangSmith) to see where time is spent and to troubleshoot failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it allows you to determine how long each of the different components take
